title: Handshake App manifest (manifest_version 1)
description: The app manifest defined by HANDSHAKE-APPS.md v0.1. Hosts validate against this schema, then apply the semantic rules the spec adds on top (capability registry, shape discrimination, signature verification). Unknown TOP-LEVEL fields are ignored for forward compatibility; unknown CAPABILITY ids make the install fail closed (spec section 4.1).

manifest_version.description: The manifest format version this document conforms to. This schema defines version 1; a host that does not recognize the version MUST refuse to install.

id.description: The app's identity: a Handshake name the author holds (dot-separated labels, each 1-63 chars, letters/digits/hyphens, no leading or trailing hyphen). Grants and shape tags are keyed by this id; authorship is proven against this name's _hns control-key anchor.

version.description: Semver, display and update-ordering only; capability diffs, not versions, drive re-consent.

handshake.description: The author's Handshake name. When present it MUST equal the manifest id.

description.description: App-supplied prose. Untrusted: consent UIs may show it only as attributed, sanitized secondary text.

tlds.description: The zones the app operates in. A ceiling, never a grant: capabilities scoped 'claimed-label' are only satisfiable by user-held names under these TLDs.

permissions.description: Non-DNS, read-only capabilities the app opts in to, as a flat {permission: level} map (HANDSHAKE-APPS.md section 5.5). v0.1 defines 'identity': 'read' — the app may read the user's MAIN identity as PUBLIC info only (native name, npub, NIP-05). A permission grants nothing unless declared here; the mediator refuses the corresponding op otherwise (opt-in and visible, never ambient). No permission ever conveys a key, a secret, or the user's other names.

identity.description: Read the user's main identity as public info only (name, native label, npub, nip05). The reference consumer is the 2url app; the mediator returns no key or secret.

cap.description: Namespaced capability id. Un-prefixed dotted ids (name.*, dns.*, content.*, identity.*) are reserved for the standard: name.claim, name.list, dns.read, dns.set-record, dns.remove-record, dns.delegate (dangerous), content.publish, identity.authenticate (mint a NIP-98 token proving control of a granted name, bound to the app's own origin — HANDSHAKE-APPS.md section 5.6; ships today as the extension one.hns.auth.nip98). Third-party ids carry a reverse-DNS namespace. A host that does not implement a declared cap MUST refuse the install.

scope.description: 'claimed-label': names under the declared tlds that the user claimed or granted through this app. 'any-held-name': any single name the user explicitly grants via the picker.

record_schema.description: REQUIRED for dns.set-record / dns.remove-record / dns.read: the key of the entry in 'records' this capability is allowed to write or read. There is deliberately no way to request a bare record type.

reason.description: App-supplied justification. Untrusted; secondary text only.

records.description: The exact record shapes the app reads/writes - its public data contract, and the namespace that isolates it from other apps. Every shape a DNS capability names MUST appear here, and every writing shape MUST carry a literal discriminator: a value prefix '<tag>=' (TXT) or an owner starting '_<tag>'.

owner.description: Owner name RELATIVE to the granted name: '@' is the granted name itself; '_tag' or '_tag.@' service prefixes; 'label.@' one level below. Never absolute, never another name's subtree. May not begin with _hns or _atproto (locked surfaces are unreachable).

type.description: One record type from the registry's USER_TYPES. NS, DS and CNAME shapes are dangerous and require the dns.delegate treatment.

template.description: The value grammar, with {field} placeholders and [optional;parts]. The mediator expands this template from propose() fields; apps never supply raw values.

prefix.description: The literal value discriminator ('<tag>='). Required for TXT shapes; the tag must be unique among installed apps and must not be a platform-reserved tag (ipfs, ar, hns, atproto, nostr, dane) unless the shape is the platform flow that owns it.

fields.description: Per-placeholder grammars the mediator validates before expansion.

grammar.description: A named field grammar the mediator implements: e.g. https-url (https only, no userinfo, no literal-IP host), ipfs-cid, arweave-txid, label, uint16, enum.

limit.description: Maximum records of this shape per granted name. Defaults to 1.

meaning.description: One sentence: what this record does. Rendered (attributed) in docs and settings, not as the consent primary.

entry.description: The app's page, and the ONLY origin that receives the window.handshake provider. Must be an origin under the app's own name (https://<id>.hns.one/, https://<label>.<id>.hns.one/, native <id> scheme URL, or a first-party browser scheme).

requires.description: Gateway serving features the app depends on, as namespaced ids. v0.1 defines one.hns.gateway.content.v1 (baseline ipfs=/ar= serving, exists) and one.hns.gateway.redirect.v1 (redirect= TXT serving, specified in HANDSHAKE-APPS.md section 10.2).

signature.description: Detached authorship proof: a BIP-340 signature by the app name's control key (anchored in the DNSSEC-signed _hns record for `id`) over the RFC 8785-canonicalized manifest with this member removed, carried as a kind-30078 event.

pubkey.description: The signing key, x-only hex. Must match the _hns anchor for `id` for the manifest to verify.

d.description: The event d-tag: 'hnsapp:<id>:<sha256 hex of the canonical manifest without signature>'.
